title: Bulk Tag Vocabulary Import Removal Delivery
summary: remove obsolete tag-registry and tag-alias import UI, modes, routes, configuration, planners, and tests after first-class creation is available
content_html:
Bulk Tag Vocabulary Import Removal Delivery

Complete Result

The Tag Registry and Tag Aliases have no bulk import controls or executable import paths. Add, merge, and replace modes are absent from the browser, Studio API, configuration, domain services, and current verification surface.

New Tag and New Alias continue through the first-class create contracts delivered by the preceding deliveries.

Dependency

First-class Tag Creation Delivery and First-class Alias Creation Delivery must both be complete before this delivery starts.

In Scope

  • Remove Tag Registry and Tag Aliases import controls, modals, upload parsing, import state, mode selection, result copy, and import-only browser modules.
  • Remove both vocabulary-import routes, dispatch, capability/config projections, request handlers, add/merge/replace planners, import normalization, and import-only summaries.
  • Remove vocabulary-import activity action registrations and current executable tests.
  • Keep historical activity evidence readable without advertising a callable import action or retaining endpoint compatibility layers.
  • Remove obsolete registry/alias import copy, selectors, service keys, and documentation.
  • Reconcile shared modules carefully so the Series Tags offline assignment-session import keeps its independently owned behavior.

Not In Scope

  • Series Tags offline assignment-session import, including its preview/apply reconciliation; its retirement is owned by Offline Tag Assignment Session Retirement.
  • Catalogue workbook, document, media, package, or other import systems.
  • Rewriting or reformatting tag-registry.json or tag-aliases.json.
  • Tag-document linking, tag schema changes, or a replacement bulk-edit tool.
  • Redirects, aliases, proxies, or dormant placeholder endpoints.

Likely Authority

  • studio/app/frontend/js/tag-registry*.js
  • studio/app/frontend/js/tag-aliases*.js
  • studio/app/frontend/js/tag-ui.js
  • studio/app/frontend/js/tag-ui-text.js
  • studio/services/tags/tag_source_model.py
  • studio/services/tags/tag_registry_mutations.py
  • studio/services/tags/tag_alias_mutations.py
  • studio/services/tags/tag_routes.py
  • studio/services/tags/tag_activity.py
  • studio/app/server/studio/studio_tag_api/registry.py
  • studio/app/server/studio/studio_tag_api/aliases.py
  • studio/app/server/studio/studio_tags_api.py
  • studio/app/server/studio/studio_app_config.py
  • studio/data/config/runtime/activity-contract.json
  • focused tag registry planner, route, runtime-config, workflow, and smoke tests

Searches must distinguish vocabulary-import ownership from the offline assignment-session and catalogue imports.

Completion And Evidence

  • /studio/tag-registry/ and /studio/tag-aliases/ have no Import controls, modals, upload state, or import modes.
  • The Studio tag API no longer registers, advertises, or dispatches either vocabulary-import endpoint.
  • Scoped source searches find no executable registry/alias import routes, handlers, planners, client endpoints, modes, or test dependencies; historical Roadmap text is not an executable dependency.
  • New Tag, New Alias, edit, delete, promotion, and demotion still work through their current first-class operations.
  • The Series Tags offline assignment-session import remains present and independently verified.
  • Existing historical activity can still be understood, while new UI/config projections expose no vocabulary-import actions.
  • The canonical registry and alias files are byte-for-byte unchanged by the removal.
  • Focused Python/service tests, JavaScript module checks, route boot/API smokes, and git diff --check support the bounded claims above.

Durable Destination

Update Tag Registry and Tag Aliases so their capabilities and workflows no longer include import. Update Tag Source Data only if the shipped write-boundary description needs to distinguish create from the retired bulk operations.
